# q3dresearch/cookbook

> Reproducible recipes that turn public records into findings. Each recipe is
> one question, one method, one figure, and a written account of what the answer
> cannot support. Python standard library only — no dependencies.

Companion to the wss-* archives at github.com/q3dresearch, which capture public
records their publishers overwrite.

## Start here
- [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md): how to reproduce, verify and extend; inherited failure modes
- [STRUCTURE.md](STRUCTURE.md): repository layout and why
- [VERSIONING.md](VERSIONING.md): method versus data versioning, append-only series

## Recipes
- [uk-company-survival](recipes/uk-company-survival/README.md): the Companies House bulk file
  is a live-register snapshot — DissolutionDate is populated on zero of the first 73,146 rows
  and every status present is one a live company holds, so the register publishes survivors and
  drops its dead. Survival becomes measurable only because the publisher keeps dated monthly
  files nothing links to: a company is dead when it stops appearing. Two-thirds gone within five
  years; agrees with ONS on ordering (rho +0.79) and not on level (below in 11 of 14 sectors);
  449,461 companies at forty formation-agent addresses survive two years at 37% against 56%
  elsewhere, 8.9 points surviving age standardisation, with the two groups indistinguishable in
  2012. Cause is explicitly not claimed: the register carries address and outcome and nothing
  about the relationship.
- [landfill-countdown](recipes/landfill-countdown/README.md): every US municipal landfill in
  one federal file, two editions three years apart. Nationally permitted room rose 14.5bn to
  14.8bn tons after burying a billion, because 1.3bn tons of new capacity went to the states
  with the shortest clocks; eight states have a median site under twenty years; two companies
  own half the remaining room. The register overwrites itself and only the current edition
  resolves, so the interval exists by accident and both workbooks are committed. Promotion
  replaced openpyxl with a stdlib xlsx reader (verified cell by cell, 2,642 rows) and that
  byte-diff exposed a figure that had never been reproducible because it iterated a set.
- [fda-gras-notices](recipes/fda-gras-notices/README.md): one dataset, eleven figures, two
  questions; merged from two recipes that read the same two FDA inventories and carried
  duplicate copies of the same classifier library, one headed "VENDORED COPY ... change it in
  both". One GRAS filing in six is withdrawn by the filer and outright refusal is 11x rarer; the
  withdrawal rate is flat at 10-21% for 28 years, but the share of pulled filings that come back
  fell from 51% before 2010 to 29% after, surviving every control run against it. Synthetic
  chemicals fail at 38% against an 11.6% base and a firm that just pulled a filing is 3.2x more
  likely to pull the next. At least 16 of 155 "never seen again" substances are still permitted,
  three via the food-additive petition route. The animal-food side of the same inventory clears
  51% against human food's 79% with every failure mode elevated, and eight firms filing on both
  sides clear 84% human against 57% animal - the programme, not the companies.
- [clinical-trial-reporting](recipes/clinical-trial-reporting/README.md): twelve figures on
  ClinicalTrials.gov's 603,730 registered studies, walked in full three times over a held-open
  connection (the host charges ~134s per connection and <1s per request; measured per request
  it reads as 135s each and the job looks impossible). FDAAA 801 requires summary results
  within 12 months of the primary completion date. Conditional hazard of reporting: 0.23% a
  month baseline, 4.59% in the deadline window (20x), 1.25% the month after, and it never
  recovers - the register exerts force on one day. On the 151,345 day-precision dates the peak
  week is 3.17% against 0.43% the next, a 7.4-fold drop, and the three most common exact lags
  are 364 days (1,621 trials), 365 and 363 - a day count, not a monthly rhythm. Completions
  from 2008-2012 already spike 22.1x against their own baseline, identical to 2017-2020, so the
  January 2017 Final Rule did not build the wall. With non-reporters kept in the denominator,
  three-year reporting rose from 20.5% (2008 completions) to ~25% by 2012 and has not moved;
  one-year tripled 5.5% to 14.7%; five-year fell. Sponsor class spans 25-fold (NIH 83.1%,
  industry 50.0%, university/hospital 17.1%, other government 3.3%) and the class that reports
  least is 75% of the register, but each class's own rate moved differently (NIH +43 points,
  industry +10, university +3, other government -2), so the flat pooled line is composition not
  stasis. The deadline spike is 82x for industry against 1.4x for other government, measured
  against each class's own baseline. THE CORRECTION TO ALL OF IT: crossing the statute's two
  applicable tests - a drug/biologic/device, and a US site - gives 67.1% (31,934 trials), 13.3%,
  17.9% and 3.4% (31,805); the effects are independent (US-site 5.0x among regulated and 5.3x
  among everything else; product 3.8x and 3.9x), and inside university sponsors alone the same
  tests give 68.8% against 5.2%. So the pooled quarter measured scope, not apathy. Also:
  UNKNOWN is a two-year staleness timer wearing a status field's clothes (8.4% of 2005
  registrations, 27.1% of 2023, 0.3% of 2025, 0.0% of 2026); 18.1-23.6% of every cohort since
  2008 was registered AFTER it finished and those trials report 3-5x less inside every class;
  terminated trials report 37.9% against completed 24.3%, and 31.6% against 16.4% inside the
  university group, which inverts the expectation that silence concentrates on failures;
  sponsor scale is a threshold not a gradient (flat 17.6-19.3% from 1 to 100 trials, then 30.9%
  and 50.0%); sample size reverses sign by class (industry 36.7 to 68.6%, universities 29.6
  down to 16.1%), so the pooled U-shape is a mixing ratio; median trial duration among finished
  trials falls 853d to 243d which is survivorship, and five-year completion actually fell 77% to
  64%; phase 2 is the bottleneck at every horizon. Product-level questions are answered
  negatively with a measured join: intervention names give 16,676 keys spanning 2+ phases across
  162,173 trials, but median within-key phase-time correlation is +0.09 because the largest keys
  are backbone agents, and the correlation decays with a key's age (+0.22 under three years,
  -0.01 past fifteen) because a drug that works re-enters phase 1 as a combination partner.
  Boundaries recorded: no compliance rate (IND/IDE never published), no cost/price/revenue field
  at all, no approval date, the enrollment actual overwrites the estimate so plan-vs-outcome
  needs version history, and /api/v2 history is 404 while /api/int history is 403. Traps: a bad
  filter fails loudly with HTTP 400 but a bad FIELD PATH fails silently with empty strings, and
  39.3% of primary completion dates carry no day of month.
- [pdb-deposition-choices](recipes/pdb-deposition-choices/README.md): nine figures on the RCSB
  PDB's 260,089 experimentally determined structures, fetched as ~200 server-side facet
  queries with no bulk download. 15.8% cite "To be published"; structural-genomics consortia
  run 74-86% of entries unwritten against that baseline while depositor size explains nothing
  (rho +0.16), and rate and volume name different leaders - JCSG 86.4% and ~1,386 entries,
  von Delft 48.7% and 2,760. The target list is an ordinary power law (R2 0.88) with the
  SARS-CoV-2 replicase only 1.6x above the fitted line, so the head is notable for which
  proteins are in it, not its height. AlphaFold shows no detectable effect on deposition,
  bounded at +/-9.9% against a pre-2021 log-linear trend. Cryo-EM's growth fitted 2012-2019 is
  +57.2%/yr at R2 0.99 and over-predicts 2025 by 74% (25,147 against 6,453) because the
  rolling three-year rate fell +65% (2018) to +9.8% (2025); two cryo-EM models crossed with
  three X-ray trajectories give six projections that all cross in 2026-2028, so respecting the
  deceleration narrows the forecast rather than widening it. The method-choice boundary moved
  from never (X-ray held 79.5% above 1000 kDa in 2005-11) to 1,532 kDa, 315, then 133 while
  the sub-50 kDa split did not move at all, which is also why NMR was never displaced.
  Resolution degrades with mass for X-ray (1.75 to 3.00 A) and is flat for cryo-EM (~3.25 A),
  and X-ray leads in every band including above 1000 kDa - from 701 structures against 5,040,
  a survivors' average that reads better the harsher the filter. A declared ADDITIVE /
  AMBIGUOUS / BIOLOGICAL ligand grouping is testable because cryo-EM never has a
  crystallisation drop: host mass correlates rho +0.94 with cryo-EM share and must be
  conditioned on, after which a linear fit says no effect (+0.5 pts, mixed signs, and it
  predicts negative shares for 8 components) while a log-odds fit says 15 of 16 additives fall
  below prediction by a median 27.7x. Three monoculture shares faceted by year separate into
  two that are practice (100 K +9.0 pts, single-particle +13.2) and one that is not (P 21 21
  21, +0.5 pts across twenty years). Traps recorded include a terms facet that returns the top
  N by count but not in count order (35 of 200), a histogram bucket read as an exact value, a
  share quoted against an unstated denominator, and a forecast scenario asserted in prose and
  never computed - all four corrected on the published plates rather than silently.
- [ocean-sampling-effort](recipes/ocean-sampling-effort/README.md): one dataset, fourteen
  figures, five questions. OBIS holds 229,671,953 marine records; 27 of 27,168 grid cells hold
  31.6% and the median cell takes 45% from a single dataset. Two fields that promise and fail:
  the WRiMS introduced flag is species-level so every species sits at exactly 0% or 100%, and
  organismQuantityType is 44 free-text strings reducing to 8 incommensurable kinds. For plants
  and single cells recorded depth is the instrument, rho +0.97 against sequencing share, with
  drill-core forams as the outlier that names the mechanism. A within-stratum composition ratio
  cancels the shared effort and yields one provable cliff at 20/30/50/70 m while three controls
  never cross; it works only where the stratum has many contributors, so the carbonate
  compensation depth is blocked, not negative. A saturating accumulation fit under-predicts
  2024 in 16 of 16 classes — no asymptote, which converts to a price differing 765-fold across
  groups. Taxonomy shows two golden ages and two world wars at -30% and -31%. Threatened species
  are better monitored than a record-count-matched control, 31.4% vs 38.4% unseen; four of five
  IUCN criteria are unreachable and B2 is ruled out for 81% of CR. Wild-capture species are
  detected at +1.04 sd and farmed species are not (p=0.36). The register's ON_LAND flag covers
  52.7% of seabird records and is a habitat map, not an error signature. Traps recorded include
  four parameters that silently return the unfiltered total, a checklist that caps at 10,000 and
  sorts by the variable being modelled, a Darwin Core schema that moved between versions, and a
  join key that matched 0 of 7,517 rows.
- [waste-route-concentration](recipes/waste-route-concentration/README.md): four counting
  artefacts in the EPA hazardous waste register, each generalising past it. The route with the
  fewest firms (deep-well injection, 31) has the lowest Gini (0.63); the one with 77 firms has
  0.98 because one company is 86% of it. Gini across all firms is flat 2001-2023 in every
  route — pin the count at each route's largest 30 and seven of eight concentrate, because
  exits come off the bottom of the distribution. A record count measures filing granularity,
  not activity: one route filed 23.8x the rows on half the tonnage. One plant is 17.0% of every
  ton the country manages. Two figures are replacements for published wrong versions, both
  kept in the write-up.
- [drug-shortage-overlap](recipes/drug-shortage-overlap/README.md): the FDA drug
  shortage register is a §506C compliance feed, not a clinical one — 137 of 196
  substances are permanent discontinuances; one reporting firm predicts an exit at
  95% vs 16%; nothing flagged for paediatric use is being discontinued (0 of 12, 8.6
  expected). Only Australia's register can support a duration and it understates it
  six-fold (median 62 days from resolved rows, 387 corrected for the twelve-month
  purge); no register keeps history. FDA's update_date is reliable (3 silent changes
  in 842) once lists are sorted and the key carries the statutory stream. Supplier
  depth, warning letters, recalls, import alerts, severity, reason codes and
  concentration were tested and failed; five superseded figures kept as worked failures.
- [hf-paper-adoption](recipes/hf-paper-adoption/README.md): which arXiv computing
  papers get adopted by someone who did not write them, and what the Hugging Face
  daily-papers feed does and does not predict about it.
- [dataset-demand-shape](recipes/dataset-demand-shape/README.md): what happens to
  a dataset published on Kaggle. 737,729 datasets; median 8 downloads; 69.5%
  never opened in a notebook; 412,935 with ten downloads or fewer. Size predicts
  use; a sample of already-successful datasets says the opposite.

## Conventions
- provenance.json records corpus hashes and the figures as computed
- history.csv is append-only; method changes are visible breaks, never edits
- if prose and script disagree, the script is authoritative
